diagram_math_checks.result: The drawing coordinates [0,2]^2 are schematic coordinates scaled by 1/2 to the physical unit square. Vertical/horizontal lines at coordinate 1 represent x=1/2 and y=1/2. Each of four squares has exactly its lower-left to upper-right diagonal: (0,0)-(1,1), (1,0)-(2,1), (0,1)-(1,2), (1,1)-(2,2). This agrees with Example line 31 and Verification step 1.1.

The standalone fresh native rendering visibly closes all four sides of the rectangle, retains both crossing grid lines and all four diagonals. Splitting at intersections gives 9 grid vertices, 16 mesh edges (8 boundary, 4 internal horizontal/vertical, 4 diagonals), and 8 closed triangles. No missing last-to-first edge occurs; rectangle and path commands were preserved. Adjacent triangles share complete edges or vertices, as required by the full matching-affine-mesh definition and step 1.1. All physical triangles have legs 1/2 and diameter sqrt(2)/2 for n=2; all n are affine scaled copies, agreeing with the local scaling supplier.

K1 is strictly inside the upper triangle of the top-left square, and K2 strictly inside the lower triangle of the bottom-right square. These are cell labels, not nodal or bubble markers. The figure is a mesh skeleton and makes no degrees-of-freedom claim: the MINI definition has continuous P1 vertex values plus one scalar interior bubble b_K=27 lambda0 lambda1 lambda2 per triangle, with vector coefficients for velocity, and continuous P1 zero-mean pressure. No diagram mark contradicts zero-boundary velocity constraints or implies pressure bubbles. Adding nodal/bubble symbols is unnecessary to repair this mesh-family illustration.

Full local Example, Verification, matching mesh definition, affine scaling lemma, MINI definition and Fortin-stability theorem were read. The domain is the bounded connected Lipschitz square, and the geometry supplies shape regularity and h_n tending to zero as in step 2.1. The existing rigorous verification and stability conclusion remain independent of the picture.
